chapter_theme: Songs at Mylapore (திருமயிலை): the poet confesses the eyes, speech and breasts of women and of the courtesans who sell love, the bad company and the deceit of his life, and his failure to think of the feet, worship or keep silence, and asks to join the devotees and see Murugan; the praise names the Goddess in long litanies, Murugan as guru who whispered into Siva's ear, and Sambandar raising the merchant's daughter at Mylai.
structure_note: Women and courtesans (689, 692, 696, 697); the poet's faults and his longing for the devotees (690, 691, 694, 695); a love-song in a girl's voice (693); and a dense song on the poison and the Lord's state (688). Songs 691 and 696 carry long litanies of names.

688.reading: The song opens with the great poison that came terrifying Brahma, Vishnu and the gods, and names the Lord of all whose instruments it fitted; the poet asks Murugan, son of Siva, to come in an instant to give him his own state. The praise names the vel thrown in the war of gods and demons, sounds the battle in drum syllables, and names Murugan, son of the Himalaya's daughter, who comes dancing on the peacock, our supreme guru dwelling at Mylai.
688.nuance: The first eight lines are a run of Sanskrit-derived words (அதகரண விதன பரிபுரண ... நிமிர சமிரமய) whose division is uncertain; they seem to speak of Siva holding the poison and of the Lord's pervasion. நினது பதவி தர வருவாயே: the plea is for Murugan's own state. Lines 11 to 12 are drum syllables.

689.reading: A short song: the poet asks whether he too must perish, stopped by women's spear-like eyes, nectar-like speech and mountain breasts. The praise names Murugan the son of Siva of Kailas, who dwells at Mylai by the waves of the sea, the lord of his devotees.
689.nuance: The three charms come in three short lines (விழியாலே, மொழியாலே, முலையாலே), and the plea is only a question, with no request.

690.reading: The poet asks that he not grow weak and his mind waste by the deceitful deeds of a great sinner without dharma, but be given the joy of living each day, worshipping the red feet and joined to grace. The praise names the vel that frightened the demons' armies, the son of the pure Abhirami, the hero whose shoulders the hunter girl longed for, and Kanda at the great city of Mylai.
690.nuance: அறமிலா அதிபாதக வஞ்சத் தொழில்: the confession is of conduct, not of women. The plea asks for a daily life (தினமுமே மிக வாழ்வுறும் இன்பம்), not release.

691.reading: In a long run of negatives the poet confesses that he does not think of the feet that end the two deeds that bring sorrow in birth, does not melt in grace, does not tire, does not worship, does not proclaim Murugan as the child Uma's lord delights in, is not filled, does not lessen his folly, does not know true insight and does not dwell in the silence where speech ends; afflicted by women, he asks whether a day will come when grace joins him to the devotees. The praise names Murugan who spoke sweet words to the hunter girl, Saravanabhava, the meaning at the end of the Vedas, the one of A, U and M and the syllables of the mantra, whose vel destroyed the demons, at Mylai of beauty and learning.
691.nuance: The confession is built from a dozen verbs ending in -கிலி (நினைகிலி, உருகிலி, அயர்கிலி, தொழுகிலி ...), a list of what devotion does by what the poet fails to do. வசனம் அறவுறு மவுனம்: silence beyond speech is among the things lacked. அகர உகர ... மகர names the parts of Om; the following சிகர ... யகர may be the syllables of the five-letter mantra, and the line is hard to divide.

692.reading: The poet describes the price-women, eyes like paired carp rolling to their earrings to wage war and sharper than Kama's arrows, breasts hung with pearls, coming like Rati, and asks whether he should wander after their gait and fall into the pit called desire. The praise names Murugan who rides the peacock with anklets ringing, whose vel split Sura in two, and who grew as the child of the mountain king's daughter, half of Siva, and came to live at Mylai.
692.nuance: விலைமானார், women with a price, names the trade, and மோகம் என்ற படுகுழி makes desire the pit the poet walks into following their gait.

693.reading: In the voice of a woman in love with Murugan, the singer asks not to waste away each night on the flower bed, seeking to ride the madal, through the arrows Kama shoots at her sandalled breasts, the slander that the women speak, and the moon circling like fire, but that Murugan come and embrace her with his shoulders on the bed. The praise names Vishnu who holds the discus and sleeps on the serpent as uncle, the hero of the green peacock at Mylai of Vedic sacrifice, and the Kumara who sang the song of grace that called back to life the girl of the merchant clan.
693.nuance: This is akam poetry, not the poet's confession: the classical torments of the lovesick girl, the gossip of women (இசைவசைகள்), the moon as fire, and the madal. அளகை வணிகோர் குலத்தில் வனிதை உயிர் மீள அழைப்ப அருள் பரவு பாடல் சொற்ற: Sambandar's raising of the merchant's daughter at Mylapore, given to Murugan, sung at the very shrine where the tradition places it.

694.reading: The poet calls himself a cruel man who, not seeking a nature unlike that of wicked gamblers who break their vows, fools who make strife, hunters of deeds and deceivers, speaks great perversity and does not keep the path, and asks that, rather than dying daily in this hut of the body, he see Murugan come on the peacock with six faces, the vel and twelve shoulders. The praise tells how Murugan shook the earth and Meru, set Sesha's hoods dancing, struck the mountain and the sea, and killed the demons so the gods regained their land, at Mylai of jack groves, lotus ponds, fields and jewelled mansions.
694.nuance: The list of vile people (சூதர், பாழ்மூடர், வினைவேடர், கபட ஈனர்) is the company the poet has resembled. The plea asks for a vision of the Lord's form (நேர்காண வருவாயே). One corrupt character in line 5 obscures a word.

695.reading: The poet asks whether, instead of wandering with worldly people on this sea-girt earth without praising Murugan, he will have a great day when, crying daily with full heart 'Son of Siva, lord of the three gods, gem of Uma, Guha', he is joined by grace to the devotees who worship. The praise tells how Indra and all the gods were humbled and the demon lords oppressed them, and how Murugan's vel split the proud Sura in two, at Mayilapuri.
695.nuance: The contrast is between two companies: உலகோரொடு திரிவேன், wandering with the worldly, and உன் அடியாராய் வழிபாடுறுவாரொடு, the worshipping devotees. The names to be cried out are given in the plea itself.

696.reading: The poet describes lovemaking at length, the breasts scented with musk and sandal, the garment slipping, the sweating face, the earrings, the bangles, the loosened hair, the anklets, the drinking of the lips, and asks whether a day will come when he, a man of deeds sunk in the whirlpool of the deep sea of the two deeds, gains grace and lives. The praise is a long litany of the Goddess, Parai, Abhinavai, Sivai, Sambhavi, Uma, Bhairavi, Tripurai, Bhagavati who holds sun and moon, the mountain's daughter, Gauri, Mohini, who never leaves Siva's side, and names Murugan her son who rides the peacock and throws the vel, at Mylai.
696.nuance: இருவினை ஈண்டும் ஆழ்கடல் இடர்படு சுழி: the two deeds are a deep sea with a whirlpool. இருகதி பெற may mean the two goals or a great goal; the sense is uncertain. The litany of the Goddess (பரை அபிநவை சிவை சாம்பவி) is longer than the praise of Murugan.

697.reading: The poet confesses that, deluded by peacock-like women with moonlike faces and unfading lust, he became the servant of those sunk in the sea of desire and of misers holding great wealth, his mind sinking like an ox, and asks, with many epithets of Murugan, whether he will gain the jewel of his grace. The praise sounds the drum in syllables, names Murugan the hero who, while Siva danced, spoke the guru's teaching with the ears covered, the son of Narayani Uma who protects the world, the master of the end of the Vedas, and the life of Mylai.
697.nuance: நீள்நிதி தரு வியலுத்தர்கள்: the poet's servitude is to misers as well as women, perhaps as a poet begging patrons. காதே மூடிய குருபோதம் உரைசெயும்: the teaching given to Siva is told as spoken with ears covered, the secret of the ear-whispered instruction, though Om is not named. The lines asking for the jewel (மாமணி ... பெறுவேனோ) are hard to divide, and two characters are corrupt.

links.note: Both are akam songs in another voice built from the classical torments of the lovesick girl, the moon and Kama's arrows; 24 is the mother's lament for her daughter, 693 is the girl's own plea that the god come to her bed.
